issue: On federal habeas review of a state court's Napue (false or uncorrected testimony) determination, must the court apply the Brecht harmless-error 'actual prejudice' standard, or does the Napue materiality standard alone govern?

sides.position: Brecht does not apply to a Napue claim; the Napue materiality standard alone governs, with no separate harmless-error analysis needed
cases: Haskell v. Superintendent Greene SCI, 866 F.3d 139, 150 (3d Cir. 2017)

sides.position: Brecht's 'actual prejudice' harmless-error standard applies to review of a Napue claim
cases: United States v. Clay, 720 F.3d 1021, 1026–27 (8th Cir. 2013)
Trepal v. Sec'y, Fla. Dep't of Corr., 684 F.3d 1088, 1111–13 (11th Cir. 2012)
Douglas v. Workman, 560 F.3d 1156, 1173 n.12 (10th Cir. 2009) (per curiam)

this_court: Does not apply Brecht separately to Napue claims; it continues to use the Napue materiality standard alone (following Hayes), and notes that applying Brecht would not change the result here
quote: We recognize, however, that the circuits have split on whether the Brecht standard applies when reviewing a state court's Napue determination.
cite: Colin Dickey v. Ron Davis, 69 F.4th 624 (9th Cir. 2023)
